recommended_title: Cap-Dependent Task Budgets for Leaderboard Promotion
central_question: On fixed public multitask score tables, how does the smallest task subset needed to make a target co-first change with the aggregation rule and the allowed fraction of score headroom?
central_thesis: In the evaluated score tables, changing the response cap reverses mean-versus-median investment orderings for some targets and makes other promotions unattainable, so aggregation-rule resistance must be reported conditional on the cap and target score vector rather than as a universal ranking.
narrative_rationale: This is a shared static score-space study with condition-specific evidence from HELM MMLU and the six-task Open LLM table, not two chronological experiments. Original final allocations contain independently bounded mean/median reversals in both settings, attainable and unattainable cases, and Borda comparisons. For HELM target row 10, mean/median costs are 9/12 tasks at full headroom and 23/12 at half headroom; for Open LLM row 1609 they are 2/3 and 4/3. These within-target comparisons support a precise conditional thesis without asserting attainable training responses or optimizer superiority. A broad solver-family story lacks ablations, a continuous-frontier story exceeds the two tested positive caps, and a search-improvement story contradicts the zero search delta. The frozen non-winning selection is still a defensible studied method: search selection and the independently completed final evaluation are different facts.
edit_framing_decision: Fresh framing, not an edit pass: no previous_paper manuscript, resolved edit-context files, aggregated directory, or extra_tasks directory was found. The required enum 'rejected' means no inherited manuscript story is adopted, not that an unseen paper was evaluated. Compare prospective cap frontiers, broad cross-setting solver improvements, and the measured cap-dependent budget story; select the last on direct evidence rather than retaining a memory-derived narrative.
staged_input_impact: Direct inspection of source_evidence/downstream/program/src/program.py and METHOD.md establishes exact scalar allocation mechanisms, bounded rival-aware Borda search, hypothetical headroom responses, and a co-first criterion. These support a score-space budget study, not new training or architecture claims.

The selected staged program source has the same file SHA-256 as ../downstream/program/src/program.py. Selection metadata directly identifies the first recorded candidate; later gain-window and mixture-cut candidates are not the studied method. Different recorded directory-tree hashes belong to different artifact scopes and are not silently equated.

source_evidence/downstream/baseline/src/program.py supplies the original comparator implementation. Its matched search score is retained as a limited selection fact, not replaced by an invented final baseline result.

Final original-case records, read independently of downstream_study, change the emphasis from prospective frontiers to two measured positive cap levels, exact reference budgets, and cap-conditioned reversals. Permutation, constant-score, and zero-update cases are controls rather than extra datasets.

The available ICLR style is single-column with a 5.5-inch text width and 9-inch text height. Its generic historical header does not authenticate an official 2026 release; the writer must verify the official venue files before final submission.

method_groups.name: Static capped-response promotion model: mean, ordinary median, and Borda
method_groups.include_reason: Defines the common scientific object: choose a target-only task subset, set selected scores to x + rho(1-x), keep rival score coordinates fixed, and minimize subset size subject to co-first tolerance. The three rules expose distinct score and rank mechanisms under the same intervention.

method_groups.name: Frozen allocation solver: exact scalar budgets and bounded rival-aware Borda search
method_groups.include_reason: This is the selected configuration actually linked to final evidence. Explain sorted gains for mean, threshold counting for odd median, endpoint counting for even median, and integer Borda gaps with a verified feasible fallback. Proposed means studied configuration, not demonstrated superiority or a novelty claim.

method_groups.name: Original frozen comparator
method_groups.include_reason: Retain the original baseline where evidence exists: study.baseline_score and study.search_score_delta establish a tied search comparison. There is no separately grounded final evaluation of that full comparator, so do not extend the comparison to final results.

method_groups.name: Evaluator-recorded no-update, random-order, and immediate-gain greedy policies
method_groups.include_reason: The final episode records contain matched task witnesses and bounds for these policies. Use no-update to expose already-co-first targets under alternative rules and use greedy/random for bounded descriptive allocation comparisons. Do not assume the evaluator's greedy policy is the original frozen baseline without an explicit implementation match.

method_groups.name: Independent exact or bounded reference allocation
method_groups.include_reason: Reference lower/upper bounds and independently checked witnesses establish what is minimal in each reported decision. In original cases the reference exact flags are true and feasible selected cardinalities match their bounds; this supports exactness for those observations, not a universal exact Borda algorithm.

results_focus: Primary comparison: paired mean and ordinary-median minimum task budgets for the same target at rho=1 and rho=0.5, separately for HELM MMLU and Open LLM. Ground every point in final.evidence.episodes, filtering solution.cases to case=original and pairing by family, target, rule, fraction, and seed.

Show both measured reversals explicitly: HELM row 10 changes from mean/median 9/12 to 23/12 tasks; Open LLM row 1609 changes from 2/3 to 4/3. These are descriptive counterexamples to a cap-independent ordering, not estimates of how frequently reversal occurs in future populations.

Report all sampled targets, including zero-cost cases and unattainable cases. Target selection is by original mean nonwinner rank, not by being a nonwinner under every rule: HELM row 40 already needs zero median updates. Do not discard it or reinterpret zero investment as an intervention effect.

Reachability under a fixed cap across all three rules: at full headroom all eight evaluated targets per family are reachable; at half headroom HELM mean/median/Borda counts are 5/5/4 and Open LLM counts are 7/6/3. The fixed denominator is eight original targets per family, not repeated seeds or controls. Use final.evidence.episodes; never count an unattainable empty witness as zero cost.

Explain solver mechanism without a superiority narrative: on the evaluated original decisions, feasible selected cardinalities match independently exact reference bounds. Matched greedy excess-task examples can illustrate threshold plateaus, such as HELM row 28 at half cap, where median needs 21 tasks versus the recorded greedy 52. Random policies have only the recorded seed/order coverage; no broad statistical claim follows.

Use matched permutation, constant-score, and zero-update controls as implementation checks only. Keep their contributions out of the scientific budget and reachability denominators; synthetic constant tables are not public empirical evidence.

Keep selection and final evidence separate: study.* records a non-winning selection, three scored attempts, zero unscored attempts, and zero search-score difference from the original baseline. final.qualification.* independently reports completed and qualified. These facts neither establish solver improvement nor establish causal training efficacy, universal validity, or unseen-family generalization.
figure_plan: Figure 1, early overview: public score table plus frozen target and rivals -> capped target-coordinate updates -> mean/ordinary median/Borda -> minimum selected-task count or unattainability. Make the counterfactual assumption and absence of model training instantly visible.

Figure 2, main paired comparison: a 2-by-2 scatter matrix, dataset by positive cap, with mean minimum task fraction on x, median minimum task fraction on y, and an equality diagonal. Plot all eight targets in each panel; handle unattainability in explicitly labeled marginal rails, not as a numeric cost. Highlight only the preidentified within-target reversal examples.

Figure 3, reachability comparison: two panels, one per dataset, with the three aggregation rules on x and the count of reachable targets out of eight on y, comparing full and half headroom. This brings Borda and lost attainability into the main paper without conflating them with finite-budget averages.

figure_specs.purpose: Give a page-1-or-2 visual definition of the score-space intervention, the common comparison design, and the distinction between a finite minimum and unattainability; use equations and labels, not fabricated example scores.
figure_specs.layout_rationale: paper.sty sets a single 5.5-inch text column, so full width equals column width; there is no two-column spanning environment to exploit. Use one horizontal conceptual panel, at most five major blocks and three rule branches, about 5.5 by 2.3 inches plus caption, occupying about 0.30 body page. Render all labels at least 9 pt. A half-width diagram would make the intervention and noncausal caveat illegible.

figure_specs.purpose: Expose the within-target cap-dependent change in mean/median budget ordering across the two evaluated score tables, retaining all finite and unattainable observations.
figure_specs.layout_rationale: At the inspected 5.5-inch single-column width, use four panels in two rows, never four across: about 5.5 by 3.8 inches plus caption, about 0.48 body page. Keep both numeric axes on [0,1], place unreachable states in separated labeled rails, and use at least 8.5-pt rendered ticks and 9-pt axis labels. Eight target points are observations, not eight colored categories or legend series. Use no more than four status encodings, annotate only the reversal exemplar in each dataset, and show multiplicity when finite points overlap. Repeated seeds must not be jittered into apparent independent target observations.

figure_specs.purpose: Compare whether promotion is possible under each rule and cap, including Borda, using the same fixed target denominator in every panel.
figure_specs.layout_rationale: Use two side-by-side panels within the single 5.5-inch text column, three rule labels and two cap markers per panel, about 5.5 by 2.0 inches plus caption or 0.26 body page. Keep a common 0-to-8 count axis and one shared cap legend at 9 pt or larger. Do not add budget averages, optimizer scores, controls, or a second definition of success to this figure.

supplementary_plan.purpose: After references, provide the exact derivations, complete paired allocation evidence, control results, and reproducibility/provenance details needed to audit the static study, without moving the central reversals, unattainability, or noncausal limitations out of the main body.

notes_for_writer: Scope of this stage: strategy only. Do not create paper.tex or claims_grounding.json, invoke final-paper validation, generate figures, or run new candidate experiments in this stage. The paper_standalone family calls for thesis-first organization, not discovery order.

Body organization and inclusive page allocation: title/abstract 0.50 page; introduction including early overview 1.00; related work 0.50; problem and intervention assumptions 0.90; allocation methods and certificate reasoning 1.35; data and comparison protocol 0.80; results including both quantitative figures and compact evidence tables 2.45; discussion and limitations 0.90; conclusion 0.35. Total target is 8.75 body pages, excluding references and substantive supplementary material. The venue accepts only 8 to 9 body pages, with page 8 at least 75 percent full if the body stops there. These are layout budgets, not empirical measurements. Do not use spacing tricks or invented experiments to reach them.

Use the page budget for scientific depth: define why task-count support is an investment proxy; derive endpoint reduction and median plateaus; distinguish odd/even medians and updated-rival Borda; show an exact cap-reversal table with separate rows for the two caps; discuss finite costs versus impossibility and the mean-based target sampling asymmetry. Keep figures near the explanations they support. If the available material still cannot fill a substantive compliant body, report insufficiency rather than add filler.

Use reader-facing section names such as Problem and Intervention Model, Allocation Certificates, Public Score Tables and Comparison Protocol, Cap-Dependent Promotion Budgets, and Scope and Limitations. The main scientific comparisons are aggregation rules under common interventions; solver baselines establish allocation context and are not the thesis.

Define x in [0,1], selected subset S, c_j(rho)=round(x_j+rho(1-x_j),10), uniform investment |S|, and normalized investment |S|/d. Co-first permits an aggregate deficit at most 1e-10; it is not strict first place. Ordinary even median averages its two middle scores. Borda is average pairwise win credit with half credit for ties, and rivals' aggregates must be recomputed after target improvement. Fixed rival coordinates do not imply fixed Borda totals.

Use only the two evaluated positive response fractions, 1 and 0.5, for the empirical cap comparison. The zero fraction belongs to the no-update control. Endpoint monotonicity supplies a model-level argument, not evidence for continuous response curves, strict-margin sensitivity, empirical-cohort ceilings, composition resampling, or actual training effects. Those experiments are absent.

Evidence mapping: use final.evidence.episodes for every main numerical allocation, count, example, and quantitative figure; the payload is paper_data.json.final_evaluation.evaluation_evidence.episodes. Use its exact episode/case/observation locations in downstream claim mapping. Method derivations additionally cite source_evidence/downstream/program/src/program.py and METHOD.md; snapshot context additionally uses task/resources/final/{helm,openllm,protocol}.json. These file paths are supporting artifacts, not newly invented grounding-source IDs.

Private-only audit context: study.selection_kind is non_winner_candidate; study.investigation_outcome is completed_no_winner; study.search_score equals study.baseline_score at 0.7239766081871346; study.search_score_delta is 0; study.attempts.total/scored/unscored are 3/3/0. final.qualification.status/outcome/correct are completed/qualified/true. final.metric.final_score is 0.6633040935672518 in a separate weighted evaluation scope. Do not subtract final and search scores or expose their internal field labels as scientific metrics. No failed final qualification is reported in this run; do not invent one or turn search non-selection into a validity failure. Missing gate-level diagnostics remain unknown.

The final evidence source marks candidate diagnostics unverified. Rely on independently recorded validation checks and reference lower/upper bounds, not candidate self-reports. Exact Borda costs can be asserted for recorded decisions with matching feasible witness size and exact reference bounds; the selected Borda algorithm itself remains deadline-bounded. Qualification is not a guarantee of novelty, causal validity, generalization, or submission completeness.

The final resource context is 57 HELM subjects and six normalized Open LLM task columns; final populations contain 42 and 2129 rows respectively. Use frozen resource metadata to document these context facts, not the task brief's broader public-catalog totals. Do not treat the six aggregate columns as six collections of all their subtask scores, and do not include Raw columns as independent tasks. Target labels in observations are local row indices, not public model identifiers; recover display names from the matching frozen resource only when needed.

Uncertainty: retain seed-level results, but distinguish execution seeds from training runs or random population samples. Selected original allocations are identical across the three recorded seeds. Report that fact and exact integer budgets rather than fabricated confidence intervals or significance tests. Random-order comparator variability can be summarized only from actual recorded orders/seeds with its small coverage stated. The eight rank-stratified mean-nonwinner targets per family are not a random sample of all models. Do not promise bootstrap, unseen-family, or composition robustness analyses absent from the artifacts.

Essential limitations belong in the abstract/method and main discussion: assumed independent capped task responses, no measured tokens/data/dollars, no transfer or forgetting, stationary rival score vectors, uniform rather than task-specific cost, co-first rather than strict win, only two positive caps, normalization-dependent comparisons, target-selection asymmetry, and finite snapshot coverage. An unattainable observation means failure under the stated score cap, not a measured training loss or algorithmic invalidity.

Planned quantitative implementation: write a downstream extractor for final.evidence.episodes that emits tidy original records and separately marked controls, verifies pairing and reference bounds, and reproduces the stated examples/counts before plotting. Collapse identical selected records across seeds only with an explicit repeatability note. Use infinity/status for impossible promotion; never use the reference d+1 sentinel as a finite budget, never average infinities away, and never score an empty unattainable allocation as zero investment.

Figure export contract: quantitative plots must be source-generated as PDF plus a 300-DPI PNG, and LaTeX must use the PDF when available. Every figure targets the inspected full 5.5-inch text column; do not treat 0.48 text width as a conference column. Use no more than three panels per row and the explicit per-figure label/series budgets. If only raster is available, regenerate from source at at least 2400 px width for these full-width figures; never upscale an existing raster.

The single required overview uses generate-concept-figure through the later orchestrator, not an agent invocation in this stage. Keep editable diagram source; obtain a vector PDF from its native diagram export when available. If only raster export is available, enforce the full-width raster floor. The overview should depict a score table and a hypothetical intervention, not a neural architecture, training pipeline, discovery timeline, or fabricated benchmark values.
